title: Warm start threshold investigation notes
content:
Context:
- Incident class: Dedicated GPU pool autoscale + capacity thrash during morning traffic spike (approx 09:30 PDT).
- Pool: dp-prod-1 (dedicated, west-2), instance type: p4d / A100-like (64GB).
- Symptoms: repeated scale-ups followed by immediate scale-downs, end-to-end latency spikes (p95 from ~120ms to >1.8s), OOM / allocation timeouts on a subset of pods, high cold-start rate.

Observations (raw breadcrumbs):
- 2024-11-03 09:27:11 PDT: first spike in incoming qps to model-id: r-instruct-13b-quant.
- 2024-11-03 09:27:21 PDT: autoscaler decision: +4 nodes (scale target -> 28) because average GPU utilization > 85% for 30s window (see HPA logs).
- 2024-11-03 09:28:05 PDT: new pods scheduled -> Pending due to imagePull/warm-init (ctx create).
- 2024-11-03 09:28:45 PDT: kubelet reports "cuda-context-create-timeout" for pod r-instruct-13b-quant-7bdf.
- 2024-11-03 09:29:02 PDT: LB starts routing traffic to new pods -> immediate error 500 for first requests (stacktrace below).
- 2024-11-03 09:29:11 PDT: autoscaler judge: nodes underutilized -> -3 nodes (scale target -> 25) because utilization averaged <40% across scaled nodes for 45s (cooldown logic kicked in).
- 2024-11-03 09:29:40 PDT: previously-warmed pods still finishing model load; latency p95 remains high; system hits request queue backlog; autoscaler sees queue and ramps again +5 nodes -> thrash.

Commands run (notes + outputs):
- kubectl get hpa -n infra dp-prod-1-hpa -o yaml  # checked thresholds and windows
  -> behavior: targetCPUUtilizationPercentage: 80, scaleUp: stabilizationWindowSeconds: 30, scaleDown: stabilizationWindowSeconds: 60
  -> custom metric is gpu_utilization (prometheus adapter), scrape interval 15s, adapter reported delays of ~10s during spike.

- kubectl describe pod r-instruct-13b-quant-7bdf -n models
  -> Events: Failed to create container: context deadline exceeded while allocating GPU resources
  -> Logs show repeated calls to cuCtxCreate and long taints on node gpu-driver-init: true

- rwinfctl pool describe dp-prod-1 --verbose
  -> pool config: warm_start_threshold=0.7, warm_start_window=20s, prewarm_count=2, max_nodes=50, min_nodes=18, scale_step=4

- PromQL (Grafana quickcheck): increase(rate(gpu_alloc_failures_total[1m])) from 09:26->09:31
  -> spike from 0.1->3.4 (per-minute rate) correlates with kube events.

- curl -sS http://model-proxy.internal/models/r-instruct-13b-quant/health
  -> response for new pod: 200 OK after ~35s from pod ready; readiness probe returned 500 initially due to kv-cache mismatch / model load incomplete.

Error snippets (copied):
- kubernetes event: "FailedCreatePodSandBox: container runtime create failed: rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = context deadline exceeded"
- app log: "model_loader.py: load_weights(): KernelAllocError: unable to mmap weights after qmapping: [Errno 12] Cannot allocate memory"
- autoscaler log: "scale_down_decision: recent_scale_up=true && stabilization_window_not_elapsed -> ignoring scale-down" (this was inconsistent with actual behavior - I saw scale-downs between warm-ups)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Warm-start threshold too low and stabilization windows misaligned with model load time. Autoscaler thinks nodes are underutilized because GPU metrics are delayed compared to request-level backlog (prometheus scrape lag + adapter latency). Result: scale-downs before pods finish warming -> thrash.
2) CUDA and model runtime have significant one-time cold-init overhead (context creation, cuDNN kernels, mapping large quantized weights). New pods may present as Ready to k8s before model is queryable (readiness probe mis-tuned).
3) Prewarm_count=2 insufficient for expected burst; prewarm placement or affinity causes both prewarmed pods to land on same physical host and not actually distribute capacity.
4) Kubernetes cluster autoscaler interacts poorly with our custom GPU metrics: step-scaling + small cooldowns produce oscillation.
5) Edge case: ephemeral driver taints during driver upgrades caused allocation delays at the same time as traffic spike (correlated with node-driver rolling upgrade job INFRA-3470).

Hypothesis evidence matrix (quick):
- Metric delay: prom adapter logs show 8-12s lag -> supports #1.
- Readiness mismatch: top-level readiness probe only checks container up, not model-loaded -> supports #2.
- Prewarm distribution: scheduling logs show prewarm pods 2x on node-15 -> supports #3.
- CA logs: scale-down happened inside our app-level autoscaler, not cluster autoscaler -> mixed for #4.
- Driver upgrade: rollout window overlapped but nodes unaffected in prior tests -> weak for #5.

Quick experiments attempted (results):
- Increased readiness probe to include /healthz/model_loaded check (temp patch) + redeploy to staging -> new pods not marked Ready until model_loaded returned true; cold-start latency visible but no immediate 500s when registering with LB.
- Temporarily bumped prewarm_count to 6 in staging -> kube scheduled across 4 nodes (spread) and initial QPS handled with fewer scale events.
- Increased scaleDown stabilization to 120s, scaleUp stabilization to 15s -> reduced oscillation in synthetic test.
- Added 10s sleep after pod Ready before LB registration (workaround) -> reduced 5xxs but added ~10s tail latency.

Notes on possible long-term fixes:
- Make readiness probe include model-loaded signal; ensure readiness only after KV cache primed and cuCtxCreate succeeded.
- Introduce a warm-start lifecycle state: pods enter WARMING state, excluded from autoscaler metrics until warmed OR register warm-weighted metrics so autoscaler understands warming capacity.
- Improve prometheus adapter latency (reduce scrape interval for gpu metrics to 10s during business hours) or use direct push metrics for hot pools.
- Leverage node-local prewarm daemonset to keep a small set of pre-initialized contexts (pinned to GPUs) to reduce first-request penalty.
- Change autoscaler policy: add request-queue length as a primary signal (not just gpu_utilization) and increase backoff/cooldown windows to >90s for GPU-backed pools.
- Pod anti-affinity for prewarm pods to avoid collocating prewarms.

Open TODOs / next steps (priority ordered):
- [P0] Patch readiness probe to include model_loaded endpoint for r-instruct-13b-quant (PR: serving-runtime#789) -> follow up with Lina on PR status.
- [P0] Add short-lived staging run with prewarm_count=6 + scaleDown=120s to validate reduction in thrash under load (owner: Jae).
- [P1] Tune prometheus adapter scrape interval for gpu metrics during peak hours (SRE consult) -> open INFRA-3512.
- [P1] Implement warm-state concept in pool controller (design doc TODO).
- [P2] Create a small node-local prewarm PoC (daemonset) to measure context create time improvements.
- [P2] Audit driver upgrade schedule to ensure upgrades don't overlap with business windows; correlate with INFRA-3470 timeline.

Quick reproduction steps (local/staging):
1) Deploy r-instruct-13b-quant image with debug flags (LOG_MODEL_LOAD=1).
2) Set pool config: min_nodes=18, prewarm_count=2 -> load generator: ramp to target qps in 30s.
3) Observe HPA and pool controller logs; capture prom adapter and kube events (kubectl get events -w).
4) Change prewarm_count and stability windows per experiment list above.

Random notes / scribbles:
- We should consider adding a "graceful-warmup" token to the LB which tells it to only send 5% of traffic initially to a warming pod, ramp to 100% after model_loaded event.
- Potential metric: "requests_handled_since_load" which would be zero until warmed. Autoscaler could interpret this as unavailable capacity.
- Watch out for memory pinning issues with quantized weights + mmap: KernelAllocError seen once; might need to bump vm.max_map_count on node image.

Conversation breadcrumbs: linked Slack thread C01234567 at 09:32 has raw stack traces and a call with SRE (notes attached). Jae did a live infra patch at 09:40 increasing prewarm_count to 4 which temporarily stabilized traffic.

If I have time next: write short design doc proposing warm-state lifecycle + autoscaler metric change and run one full production dry-run during low-traffic window.

End of notes.
